# EnterpriseGlue v0.32.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.31.1`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This release contains compatibility changes that require the upgrade guidance below.

## Highlights

- **security:** Use one application-issued, signed and session-bound XSRF-TOKEN cookie echoed in the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.
- **oracle:** Make the historical database migrations replay safely on Oracle and PostgreSQL, so partially populated Oracle schemas no longer fail with ORA-00902 or ORA-01758, and nullability or type changes keep existing data.
- **runtime:** Use vendor-patched zlib runtime packages across application and bootstrap images and remove the expired CVE-2026-85091 scanner exception.

## User and administrator impact

- Browser API requests use one readable application token cookie and one request token header, including after session and token rotation.
- Oracle databases that replay the historical migration epoch no longer stop with ORA-00902 (invalid datatype) or ORA-01758 (table must be empty to add mandatory column).
- Migrations that relax or tighten NOT NULL on populated Oracle tables change the column in place instead of dropping and re-adding it, so role-assignment and deployment-lineage data is preserved.
- Oracle installations whose Camunda native-grant import evidence was stored as VARCHAR2 are widened to CLOB without losing the stored classifications or encrypted snapshots.
- Application and managed-shard bootstrap images use corrected vendor libraries with matching package metadata; application interfaces are unchanged.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Deploy frontend and backend together and reload existing browser tabs.
- Update API clients to echo XSRF-TOKEN in X-XSRF-TOKEN instead of csrf_secret and X-CSRF-Token. Token endpoint paths and JSON response fields are unchanged.
- For split frontend/API subdomains, set the backend EG_XSRF_COOKIE_DOMAIN to the narrowest trusted shared parent domain or use a same-origin proxy.

## API and integration compatibility

- Protected cookie-authenticated API clients must echo XSRF-TOKEN in X-XSRF-TOKEN. Cookie/header equality, cryptographic signature and session binding are required.

## Configuration

- Cookie/header names are fixed to XSRF-TOKEN and X-XSRF-TOKEN; there is no separate gateway token or configurable header-name mode.
- Optional backend EG_XSRF_COOKIE_DOMAIN controls the readable cookie scope; the default is host-only.
- No environment variables or deployment configuration changes are required; Oracle datatype repair is performed by the historical migrations.

## Database migrations

- Migration: CleanupLegacyInvitationsSchema1700000000013.
- Migration: RequireCanonicalRoleAssignmentShape1700000000084.
- Migration: MakeRoleAssignmentAliasesOptional1700000000046.
- Migration: AddDeploymentHistoryLineage1700000000058.
- Migration: WidenCamundaNativeGrantEvidence1700000000100.
- Existing migrations were corrected in place; no new migration is added and already-applied migrations are not re-run.
- Legacy migrations resolve column types for the connected database. PostgreSQL schemas built from text columns receive the same DDL as before.
- Nullability changes clone the live column, so Oracle receives MODIFY ... [NOT] NULL and PostgreSQL receives ALTER COLUMN ... SET/DROP NOT NULL with data intact.
- Migration 013 changes only nullability on live invitation alias columns, preserving their existing types and values on MySQL as well as Oracle.
- Defaults do not imply index-key sizing: non-indexed text, including SSO JSON documents, retains the established document width of 4000 (4096 on Spanner; text on PostgreSQL).
- On Oracle, migration 100 widens VARCHAR2 evidence to CLOB through a staging column (add, copy, drop, rename). Each step checks the live schema; a rerun after the rename also restores the canonical required classifications constraint.
- A bootstrap that runs synchronize() before replaying the epoch still stops at AddReleaseEffectCohorts1700000000131 by design; that schema-epoch guard is unchanged.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: no.

## Security

- The existing signed, session-bound validator remains active; cookie-only, mismatched, forged and foreign-session tokens are rejected.
- Authentication cookies remain HttpOnly. Only the application XSRF token cookie becomes JavaScript-readable.
- The transport rereads the cookie for each request and retry, rejects ambiguous/malformed values, restricts token delivery to the configured API origin and rejects redirects.
- Editor snapshot requests encode project and query-supplied commit identifiers as path segments.
- The backend, frontend, and managed-shard bootstrap images require signed Chainguard zlib 1.3.2.1_rc20260921-r0 or later; the backend no longer overwrites the older package with a custom library build.
- CVE-2026-85091 is no longer suppressed; the existing scanner and all-severity application image gates are unchanged.

## Known limitations

- Split frontend/API subdomains require a suitable explicitly configured shared cookie domain or a same-origin API proxy.
- Independently gateway-issued tokens are unsupported. Same-session token renewal does not revoke older valid pairs independently of the authentication session.
- A schema-epoch bootstrap that has already created release_effect_cohorts through synchronize() is still refused by migration 131 on every database.

## Rollback

- Roll frontend and backend back together and restore API clients to the previous cookie/header contract. Clear cookies left by the changed deployment.
- Redeploy the previous shared package or application image. Widened Oracle CLOB evidence columns and relaxed or tightened nullability are retained; automatic schema shrinking is unsupported.
- Restoring an older image also restores its earlier zlib package and scanner exception; prefer a forward fix. No database rollback is needed.

- Chromium integration across app.xsrf.test and api.xsrf.test passed with the actual frontend transport and backend CSRF middleware/issuance helpers: a single application cookie, HttpOnly authentication cookies, login/refresh/session rotation, explicit header proof, CORS, logout cleanup and redirect leakage prevention.
- Disposable physical PostgreSQL session qualification passed again after the test-harness corrections: 45 tests. No persistence or database schema changed.
- Shared, plugin-runtime, backend-host, frontend-host and production frontend builds and the frontend bundle budget passed.
- All five plugin/API and three host tarballs passed dependency and exported-entrypoint checks; the isolated packed backend-host runtime import passed.

- Full backend unit gate passed after integrating current main: 476 files / 3882 tests, plus seven build-resolver tests and the raw-SQL guard. Regression tests cover IPv4/IPv6 listeners sharing one port and isolation of OpenAPI contract mutations.
- Prior intermittent route failures were traced to Supertest connecting to an unrelated IPv4 service while its owned listener used IPv6; the test setup now preserves the listener address family. OpenAPI suites generate the static contract once and clone it for each check, and backend workers are bounded at four. Security assertions and time limits remain unchanged.
- Regression coverage uses the real MySQL query runner in SQL-memory mode to reject DROP/ADD during invitation alias nullability changes.
- Migration tests cover SSO JSON document capacity on all five dialects and Oracle widening retries after both the drop and committed rename steps.
- Physical database, compiled-upgrade, and aggregate CI qualification are retained as separate revision-specific run artifacts.
- CI contracts passed: 207 tests; release-note preflight passed: 169 tests, semantic version recommendation, fragment validation and documentation boundary.
- The 34 pooled-tenancy/bootstrap contracts passed, and the rebuilt bootstrap image passed real PostgreSQL creation, idempotence, bounded receipts, and drift-rejection qualification.
- Backend runtime-base, full frontend, and full managed-shard bootstrap images built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Non-root Node gzip checks passed for backend and bootstrap; actual Nginx gzip delivery of the built JavaScript bundle passed on both frontend architectures.
- The pinned release scanner and current vulnerability database reported zero unignored findings at all severities on all six locally checked images, with the zlib exception removed. Full protected CI and exact-candidate qualification remain separate requirements.
